hits.text: Section 3: Class Attendance & Leave of Absence 3.1 Mandatory Attendance Standards and Classroom Engagement Active participation and regular physical classroom attendance are vital components of the participatory pedagogical philosophy at VinUniversity. Attendance is rigorously tracked across all lecture, seminar, discussion group, laboratory, and clinical sessions. Undergraduate students are required to maintain a minimum attendance rate of 80% of all scheduled instructional contact hours in each enrolled course. Failure to achieve 80% attendance without approved medical or university-sanctioned excused absence results in immediate academic disqualification from sitting the final course examination. Students disqualified for excessive absenteeism automatically receive a failing course grade of 'F' with 0.0 grade points, which is computed into both the semester and cumulative grade point averages. Instructors must issue formal written warnings to students whose cumulative unexcused absences exceed 10% of total contact hours. Tardiness exceeding 15 minutes past the scheduled class start time is recorded as a half-absence; three recorded tardies equal one full instructional absence in official attendance accounting.

Section 3: Class Attendance & Leave of Absence 3.2 Excused Absence Criteria and Documentation Protocol The university recognizes specific extenuating circumstances under which absences from instructional sessions may be designated as officially excused, preventing penalty against the 80% attendance threshold. Approved excused absences encompass documented acute medical illness or injury, significant bereavement involving immediate family members (parents, siblings, grandparents), mandatory legal obligations, and official participation in university-sanctioned athletic or academic competitions authorized by the Vice Provost of Academic Affairs. To obtain an excused absence, the student must submit an electronic Absence Request along with verifiable supporting documentation (such as hospital discharge certificates, medical certificates from Vinmec, or court summons) through the student portal within three business days of returning to campus. Even with verified excused absences, a student who misses more than 35% of total instructional contact hours in a course cannot receive a passing grade due to inadequate experiential exposure and must repeat the course in a subsequent term.

Students must achieve a minimum cumulative GPA (CGPA) of 2.00 on a 4.00 scale across all courses attempted. A strict Academic Residency Requirement mandates that at least 50% of the total credits required for the degree (minimum 64 credits), including all 3000-level and 4000-level major core courses, must be completed in direct residency at VinUniversity. A course withdrawal results in a permanent recorded grade notation of 'W' on the student's official academic transcript. The 'W' grade carries no grade point weight and does not impact cumulative GPA calculation; however, tuition fees paid for withdrawn courses are entirely non-refundable. Students may not withdraw from a course if such withdrawal reduces their semester credit load below the mandatory 12-credit full-time minimum, unless granted medical leave by University Health Services. A student is permitted a maximum of three 'W' grades across their entire undergraduate tenure. All course prerequisites specified in the University Course Catalog are programmatically enforced by the Student Information System. Waivers for prerequisites require concurrent approval from the course instructor, Program Director, and College Curriculum Committee.

Section 8: Tuition Schedule & Scholarships 8.5 Need-Based Financial Aid and Tuition Refund Schedule Students with demonstrable financial hardship may apply for Need-Based Financial Aid to supplement merit scholarships. Financial aid applications require certified tax returns, household income documentation, and bank statements submitted annually to the Financial Aid Office. Need-based aid awards range from 20% to 80% of remaining tuition liability and may include on-campus student work-study stipends providing up to 20 hours per week of paid administrative or research assistantship employment. For students who officially withdraw from the university during an active semester, tuition fee refunds are strictly prorated according to the following schedule: (1) Withdrawal during Week 1-2 (Add/Drop Period): 100% tuition refund less non-refundable deposit; (2) Withdrawal during Week 3-4: 50% tuition refund; (3) Withdrawal during Week 5-6: 25% tuition refund; (4) Withdrawal after Week 6: 0% refund (no refund). Residential dormitory fees and university dining plan charges are non-refundable after the conclusion of the second week of the semester.

Section 3: Class Attendance & Leave of Absence 3.4 Re-enrollment After Leave and Administrative Withdrawal To resume active degree studies following an authorized Leave of Absence, the student must submit a formal Intent to Return Notice to the Registrar no later than 30 calendar days before the start of the intended semester. If the leave was granted for medical or psychological reasons, re-enrollment is strictly conditional upon submitting a comprehensive fit-for-study medical clearance evaluation signed by an accredited specialist physician and validated by the VinUniversity Health Center. Students who fail to submit the Intent to Return Notice or fail to register for courses by the end of the Add/Drop Period following the expiration of their approved leave are deemed to have abandoned their studies and will be subject to Administrative Withdrawal. An administratively withdrawn student seeking readmission must undergo the complete competitive admissions process de novo as a fresh applicant and cannot automatically reinstate previous scholarship commitments.
